name: Outrider
desc: Develops autonomous electric yard truck systems that move trailers in distribution yards for large shippers and retailers.
markets: Enterprise distribution yards in the United States; 2026 YMX Logistics partnership targets US deployments; no verified international activity.
rationale: B2B autonomy technology for US logistics yards; little brand marketing and no international footprint, so F1 fit is weak.

name: 7AI
desc: Sells an agentic AI security operations platform whose AI agents triage and investigate alerts for enterprise security teams.
markets: Enterprise customers in financial services, retail, technology and healthcare, US-based; no verified international offices or expansion plans.
rationale: Several cybersecurity rivals sponsor F1 teams; a young US-focused vendor could use B2B hospitality, but scale and reach are limited.

name: Antithesis
desc: Provides deterministic simulation testing software that finds and reproduces bugs in distributed systems for engineering teams.
markets: Customers include Jane Street, MongoDB and Ethereum developers; no verified international offices or expansion plans found.
rationale: Niche developer tool with little brand marketing; F1 engineering reliability story is a loose tie-in, so fit is weak.

name: Endor Labs
desc: Sells application security software that finds and prioritises risks in open-source dependencies and code for engineering teams.
markets: Offices in Palo Alto, Delft (Netherlands) and Bengaluru (India); enterprise customers in US tech and finance; reseller in Azerbaijan.
rationale: Cybersecurity rivals already sponsor F1; offices across US, Europe and India suit B2B hospitality for enterprise security buyers.

name: Luminary Cloud
desc: Offers a cloud physics AI and simulation platform that speeds engineering design for aerospace, automotive and sporting goods makers.
markets: Named customers are US firms such as Joby Aviation, Otto Aviation, Piper Aircraft and Trek Bikes; no verified international offices.
rationale: Aerodynamics simulation is a natural F1 technology showcase, though the company is young and US-focused with limited marketing budget.

name: Pryon
desc: Sells enterprise AI knowledge management and retrieval software that answers questions from an organisation's documents for businesses and government.
markets: Enterprise and government customers such as Dell, NVIDIA and Westinghouse, US-focused; no verified international offices or expansion plans.
rationale: B2B AI vendor could use hospitality with enterprise buyers, but US focus and modest scale make F1 a weak fit.

name: Virtru
desc: Provides email and file encryption and data-centric security software for government, defence, healthcare and financial organisations.
markets: Thousands of customers, marketed in North America, Europe and Asia; staff in US, Canada, France, South Korea and Philippines.
rationale: Security rivals sponsor F1; international enterprise and public-sector buyers could be reached through hospitality, though the brand is niche.

name: Eve
desc: Builds an AI platform for plaintiff law firms covering case intake, document review, drafting and discovery, sold by subscription.
markets: Serves several hundred US plaintiff law firms such as Mike Morse Law Firm; no verified international activity or plans.
rationale: Sells only to US plaintiff law firms; a global motorsport audience offers little commercial value, so F1 fit is weak.

name: Ripcord
desc: Uses robotic scanning systems to digitise paper records into searchable data for enterprises and government agencies.
markets: Enterprise and US government clients including an IRS pilot; robotic scanning facilities reported in the US and Japan.
rationale: Robotics and AI data story could suit a technology showcase, but B2B services brand with modest marketing; weak-to-plausible fit.

name: Alianza
desc: Provides a cloud communications platform that telecom operators use to deliver branded voice, messaging and business phone services.
markets: Company reports over 1,000 service-provider customers in 80+ countries, mainly North America; acquired Metaswitch from Microsoft in 2025.
rationale: Sells to telecom operators worldwide; F1 hospitality could reach operator executives, though the brand is invisible to consumers.

name: AtScale
desc: Sells a semantic layer platform that gives enterprises consistent business metrics across data warehouses, BI tools and AI.
markets: Large enterprise customers such as Fidelity, Home Depot and Cardinal Health; R&D centre in Sofia, Bulgaria; no full country list.
rationale: Data analytics vendor could pair with F1 data storytelling for enterprise hospitality, but brand is niche; plausible, not obvious.

name: Point Wild
desc: Owns consumer and business online protection brands including Total AV, Hotspot Shield, UltraAV and Betternet, sold by subscription.
markets: Company fact sheet reports customers in 150 countries; UK operations from Total Security; consumers and enterprises worldwide.
rationale: Consumer antivirus and VPN brands with worldwide subscribers; F1's global consumer audience suits brand marketing, and security rivals sponsor teams.
changed: Formed by merger of Pango Group and Total Security, renamed Point Wild in December 2024

name: Prophecy
desc: Offers a visual, AI-assisted platform for building and managing data pipelines on Databricks and other cloud data platforms.
markets: Offices in California and India (Bengaluru, Gurugram); Fortune 500 customers in finance, healthcare, retail and technology.
rationale: B2B data tooling with little brand marketing; F1 data tie-in exists but the company is small, so fit is weak-to-plausible.

name: Blackwall
desc: Sells web traffic and bot protection security that hosting and infrastructure providers resell to protect customer websites.
markets: Customers include defence ministries of Canada and seven European NATO states; plans expansion across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Middle East.
rationale: Fast-growing security firm expanding across four regions; cybersecurity rivals sponsor F1, so a partnership could build brand awareness.
changed: Renamed from BotGuard to Blackwall in 2025

name: authID
desc: Provides biometric face-based identity verification and passwordless authentication software for enterprises, retailers and financial firms.
markets: US enterprise and retail customers; deployed in Japan through NEC subsidiary NESIC; partners MajorKey and Trinsic sell globally.
rationale: Small listed security vendor with limited marketing budget; identity security rivals sponsor F1, but fit is only plausible.

name: DOOR (Latch, Inc.)
desc: Provides smart access hardware, software and automated services for multifamily residential buildings and their owners and residents.
markets: Residential building owners, operators and residents in the United States; no verified international activity or expansion plans.
rationale: US multifamily building technology with a domestic customer base; global motorsport audience offers little value, so F1 fit is weak.
changed: Latch, Inc. now operates as DOOR; headquarters moved from New York to St. Louis

name: BetterCloud
desc: Sells SaaS management software that automates employee onboarding, offboarding, access and security across workplace applications for IT teams.
markets: Now part of CoreStack, whose group serves over 2,000 customers and partners globally across 40+ countries; BetterCloud's own split not published.
rationale: Mid-size B2B IT software unit inside a governance group; limited brand marketing makes F1 only a plausible hospitality play.

name: Clari
desc: Sells AI revenue platform software for sales forecasting, pipeline management and deal tracking to mid-size and large companies.
markets: Combined Clari + Salesloft serves over 5,000 customers such as Adobe, IBM, 3M and Shopify; no verified country breakdown found.
rationale: Enterprise sales software sold to revenue leaders; F1 hospitality suits B2B selling, and CRM rival Salesforce already sponsors F1.
changed: Merged with Salesloft in December 2025; combined company reportedly adopted the Salesloft brand in 2026 (unconfirmed)

name: Alpheya
desc: Provides an AI-based wealth management technology platform for banks, asset managers and advisers serving wealthy clients in the GCC.
markets: Serves banks, asset managers and advisers in the GCC region; new office planned in Al Ain, Abu Dhabi.
rationale: Gulf fintech backed by Lunate and BNY; Abu Dhabi Grand Prix hospitality could reach regional bank clients, but brand is small.

name: Immuta
desc: Provides data security and access governance software that controls sensitive data across cloud data platforms for large organisations.
markets: US offices plus London European base serving UK, France, Italy, Germany and Sweden; customers include Roche, Swedbank, Mercedes-Benz Group.
rationale: Enterprise data security vendor with US and European customers; security rivals sponsor F1, so hospitality is plausible.

name: Gladly
desc: Sells AI-assisted customer service software giving agents a unified view of each customer, used by retailers and consumer brands.
markets: Customers are mainly US retailers and consumer brands; listings show product availability abroad, but no verified international offices.
rationale: Customer service software for consumer brands; modest marketing scale and US focus make F1 a plausible-to-weak fit.

name: Vega
desc: Sells an AI-native security analytics platform that detects and investigates threats across distributed data without centralising it.
markets: Offices in Tel Aviv and New York; customers reportedly include Fortune 500 firms, banks and a healthcare organisation.
rationale: Young security analytics vendor; cybersecurity rivals sponsor F1, but limited scale and marketing make fit plausible, not obvious.

name: MakinaRocks
desc: Sells industrial AI software, including its Runway platform, for manufacturing anomaly detection and process optimisation to large manufacturers.
markets: Korean manufacturers such as Samsung, Hyundai Motor and LG; Japanese subsidiary since 2025 with automotive and machinery customers.
rationale: Industrial AI for automotive makers could fit a technology tie-in, but Korea-Japan focus and small scale limit F1 value.

name: Auros
desc: Provides customer insight, user research and human AI evaluation services through its UserTesting and User Interviews product brands.
industry: human insight and AI data services
markets: Participant network of over 7.6 million verified people across 34 core markets; customers are product, marketing and AI teams.
rationale: Rebranded company seeking awareness among marketing and AI teams; F1 could support a brand launch, though fit is plausible only.
changed: Formerly UserTesting; renamed Auros in September 2026; Thoma Bravo portfolio company
